MARKET.head: Australian white wine shipments to China more than double in third quarter
MARKET.summ: White wine export volumes to the market more than doubled, rising 143.6%, according to Wine Australia data. The growth comes as Australian producers seek a greater foothold among Chinese white wine drinkers, including consumers exploring alternatives to Burgundy
takeaways: Australian wine export value to mainland China rose 1.9% in Q3 2026 while global exports fell 7.3%.
White wine export volumes to mainland China jumped 143.6% in the quarter, to 5.26 million liters, per Wine Australia data.
White wine still made up only 7.14% of Australian export value to mainland China, against 91.62% for red.

MARKET.head: VinePair roundup covers Stoli, Modelo, spending, Heineken, RNDC and Diageo news
MARKET.summ: This is VinePair’s Booze News Weekly Roundup, where we gather the hottest headlines and product releases every Friday for a snapshot of what’s happening in the beverage alcohol industry. This week, we have updates on Stoli’s return to the U.S., Modelo’s deal with the NCAA, the latest product releases, and more.
takeaways: VinePair's weekly roundup gathers beverage alcohol headlines and product releases, including Stoli's return to the U.S. and Modelo's NCAA deal.
Other items cover Heineken's memo on weight-loss drugs and drinking, and RNDC's Chapter 11 liquidation.
The roundup also reports Diageo's toxic chemical spill, SCOTUS reviewing a home distilling case, and EU approval of Chianti rosé.

MARKET.head: Hampshire wineries Chalkdown and The B58 launch joint celebration wine collective
MARKET.summ: Chalkdown English Sparkling Wine and The B58 Winery, two of Hampshire’s independent winemakers, are launching the Hampshire Celebration Collective, a new partnership created to bring local wines to the county’s
takeaways: Chalkdown English Sparkling Wine and The B58 Winery, two Hampshire producers, are launching the Hampshire Celebration Collective partnership.
The launch is a free tasting at Kingsgate Wines & Provisions in Winchester on Thursday 19 November, 5pm to 7pm.
The Collective offers bespoke pricing per order, mix-and-match wines, and a minimum order of one case.

MARKET.head: Shanghai wine trader WINEXSH files for bankruptcy liquidation amid price slump
MARKET.summ: Shanghai-based fine wine trader WINEXSH has applied for bankruptcy liquidation, with a supplier reporting an unpaid order and Chinese wine media citing complaints from customers unable to collect wines or secure refunds
takeaways: Shanghai Free Trade Zone Wine Exchange Co., known as WINEXSH, applied for bankruptcy liquidation, with a notice published October 17.
The Shanghai Pudong New Area People's Court held a hearing on the application October 29; acceptance is not yet confirmed.
A Bordeaux supplier says WINEXSH left its latest en primeur order unpaid, amid falling Chinese fine wine prices and large inventories.

MARKET.head: Western Australian wineries sell well at two-day Shanghai festival
MARKET.summ: A two-day Discover Western Australian Festival drew nearly 900 people in Shanghai, with exhibitors reporting stronger-than-expected consumer sales and new business prospects among distributors, restaurants and hotels
takeaways: Discover Western Australia Festival in Shanghai on November 7-8 drew nearly 900 people, including about 600 consumers and 300 trade professionals.
Twenty exhibitors, including 17 wineries from Margaret River and Great Southern, sold wines on site and through Red Note.
Distributors including For U Global and Pran Wines reported strong buyer interest, with some sales limited by lack of stock.

MARKET.head: Wine Australia and Wine Victoria fund three-year Victorian wine industry projects
MARKET.summ: A new partnership between Wine Australia and Wine Victoria will fund a range of projects across the Victorian wine industry supporting grapegrowers and winemakers.
takeaways: Wine Australia and Wine Victoria will co-fund three-year projects supporting Victorian grapegrowers and winemakers, aligned with the Victorian Wine Strategy 2025-2030.
The program combines $540,000 in Victorian Government funding secured by Wine Victoria with $346,667 from Wine Australia's AWFF.
Projects target sustainability, biosecurity, data-driven decisions and export capability, delivered through workshops, webinars, benchmarking tools and consumer insights.

MARKET.head: Wine stays Australia's top-bought alcohol as drinking moderates and spending per visit rises
MARKET.summ: New research shows that wine endures as “the most widely purchased category” in Australia at 55%, followed by spirits at 46% and beer at 44%. The new ‘What’s Driving Australia’s Alcohol Shopper: Consumption, Channels, Promotions and Occasions’ report from Vypr and Shop! ANZ found that 41% of Australians are drinking less than a...
takeaways: A Vypr and Shop! ANZ report found wine is the most purchased alcohol category in Australia at 55% of shoppers.
41% of Australians are drinking less than a year ago or have stopped, while only 6% are drinking more.
48% of shoppers now typically spend over $40 per liquor-store visit, up from about 23% a year ago.

MARKET.head: Moldova pitches indigenous grapes and competitive prices at ProWine Shanghai
MARKET.summ: With 23 wine and spirits producers heading to ProWine Shanghai, the export-driven country is putting indigenous grapes and competitive pricing at the center of its pitch
takeaways: 23 Moldovan wine and spirits producers will seek business with Chinese importers at ProWine Shanghai, November 10 to 12.
Chinese customs data show Moldovan wine imports reached US$1.43 million in the first nine months of 2026.
About 85% of Moldova's wine production is exported, and the European Union takes roughly 60% of its wine exports.

MARKET.head: Australian wine's small formats gain ground as moderation and single-person households grow
MARKET.summ: Consumer demand for wine is changing globally, and while this has shown up in many mature markets as a decline in consumption, the shift in consumption habits has also uncovered an increasing consumer interest in smaller, more flexible packaging formats.
takeaways: Combined export and domestic off-trade sales of 187mL packs rose 22% to almost 1.9 million litres in 2025-26.
Export volumes of 187mL packs grew 39% from 450,000 litres in 2023-24 to 620,000 litres in 2025-26.
Census data shows 26% of Australian households are now single-person, up from 18% in 1981.

MARKET.head: EU greenwashing directive takes effect, forcing wine labels to drop vague eco claims
MARKET.summ: New restrictions on environmental marketing claims are putting terms like “natural” and “eco-friendly” under the microscope, prompting questions about what wineries can and can’t include on bottle labels
takeaways: EU Directive 2024/825, also called EmpCo, bans vague environmental claims like 'eco-friendly' and 'green' from wine marketing from September 27.
Unbacked sustainability badges and irrelevant claims are prohibited, and old stock is not grandfathered, so producers use stickers or point-of-sale notices.
Enforcement is left to individual member states, with fines of up to four percent of annual turnover for widespread violations.

MARKET.head: Bordeaux takes 41% of traded value as Burgundy's share jumps
MARKET.summ: Bordeaux strengthened its lead of the market, claiming 41% of traded value. Burgundy’s share also rose compared to last week
takeaways: Bordeaux claimed 41% of the week's traded value, with 2019 and 2020 vintages the top sellers by value.
Burgundy's share rose from 15.7% to 20.8%, with Domaine de la Romanee-Conti and Domaine Leflaive leading its trade.
Champagne's share fell from 13.0% to 8.5% and Tuscany claimed 11.6%, according to Liv-ex market data.

CULTURE.head: VinePair's Keith Beavers reflects on American wine in 2026 and how to keep celebrating it
CULTURE.summ: This episode of Wine 101 is brought to you by Wines of Alsace and Alsace Rocks. Tucked between the Vosges Mountains and the Rhine River in northeastern France, Alsace is one of the most distinctive wine regions on earth, and is home to centuries of family winemaking, some of France’s most certifiably organic vineyards, and a...
takeaways: Keith Beavers, host of VinePair's podcast Wine 101, reflects on American wine in 2026.
He suggests ways to keep celebrating U.S.-made wine going forward.

CULTURE.head: ASVO names 2026 Viticulturist and Winemaker of the Year at awards dinner
CULTURE.summ: Last night, the Australian Society of Viticulture and Oenology (ASVO) revealed the winners of its Awards for Excellence. The ASVO said the winners were chosen from a very high calibre and diverse range of submissions showing expertise across winemaking, viticulture and wine science. Highlights of the evening included the naming...
takeaways: The Australian Society of Viticulture and Oenology named its 2026 Viticulturist of the Year as Chris Dent, owner of Gorton Drive Estate vineyard near Swan Hill.
David Bicknell of Oakridge Wines, with nearly 25 years at the winery, was named 2026 Winemaker of the Year.
Tracey Siebert, AWRI flavour scientist, received the Wine Science and Technology Award; Sarah Lavelle of Seven Hill Cellars won the Emerging Talent Award.

CULTURE.head: AI's energy, e-waste and water footprint threatens wine's green reputation
CULTURE.summ: The Australian and New Zealand wine sector prides itself on sustainability. The very concept has become the industry’s bread and butter, quite frankly. Look at any winery website and you’ll find a dedicated page filled with paragraphs detailing all the initiatives reducing carbon emissions, saving water and limiting energy use...
takeaways: Australian and New Zealand wineries heavily promote sustainability, but AI-generated wine marketing and labels could undermine that clean reputation.
Data centres powering AI could consume up to 5 million gallons of water per day and are increasingly drawing on drought-stressed aquifers.
AI infrastructure could generate up to 2.5 million tonnes of e-waste yearly by 2030, according to a United Nations University study.

CULTURE.head: Marlborough viticulturist Anna Kelland wins 2026 Young Horticulturist of the Year
CULTURE.summ: Marlborough viticulture technician Anna Kelland has won the Young Horticulturist of the Year title, having “excelled” in an intensive two-day competition in Auckland from 4-5 November. Kelland was the 2025 New Zealand Young Viticulturist of the Year and therefore went through to represent the viticulture sector in this year’s...
takeaways: Marlborough viticulture technician Anna Kelland won the Young Horticulturist of the Year title at a two-day Auckland competition on 4-5 November.
Kelland, the 2025 New Zealand Young Viticulturist of the Year, also won three awards including the Woolworths Innovation Project Award.
Her prizes total more than $25,000, including a professional development scholarship and a glass trophy.

SCIENCE.head: Burgundy estate maps soil conductivity to guide vineyard decisions
SCIENCE.summ: Electrical conductivity maps can reveal striking differences beneath seemingly uniform vineyards, but understanding what those differences mean is far more complicated
takeaways: Domaine du Cellier aux Moines in Givry, Burgundy, used electrical conductivity mapping from 2021 to guide digging of over 30 soil pits.
Pinot Noir parcels with the same clone reached 14.5% and 13.6% potential alcohol after trimmed versus tressed canopy management.
A 2025 Médoc study by geophysicist Myriam Schmutz found the strongest vine links around 50 centimeters deep, varying by season.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Vinography Unboxed: Week of 11/8/26
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Hello and welcome to my weekly dig through the pile of wine samples that show up on my doorstep, asking

NEWSLETTERS.head: Portuguese mini-study: four red wines from Casa Ferreirinha, Quinta Nova, Douorum and Rocim
NEWSLETTERS.summ: These four Portuguese reds were all purchased from supermarket Pingo Doce and an independent wine shop, while I was teaching
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Four Portuguese reds were tasted, bought from supermarket Pingo Doce and an independent shop while the author taught in Vila Real.
Casa Ferreirinha Vinha Grande 2023 Douro scored 92/100 and Quinta Nova Unoaked 2024 Douro scored 93/100.
Tons de Duorum Talhão 37 2024 Douro, a Pingo Doce private label from Duorum, scored 91/100 at €6.99, while Rocim's Alicante Bouschet 2024 Alentejo scored 89/100.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Five Minutes with... Rick Rainey & Léana Godard of Forge Cellars
NEWSLETTERS.summ: On Cabernet Franc’s untapped potential, giving Finger Lakes terroir a seat at the table, and why it’s all about joy
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Forge Cellars, founded 2011 on Seneca Lake in New York's Finger Lakes, began making Cabernet Franc with the 2019 vintage.
Forge makes four single-vineyard Cabernet Francs from different soils, including Willow (sand), Railroad (gravel), Arlo (clay) and Bellows (sand and rock).
In 2023 Forge left stems out entirely to read each site's tannin potential, then reintroduced stems in some wines in 2024.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Kitchen Season’s Pantry Staples
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Stocking up before the cooking starts in earnest; plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Meg Maker's Maker's Table pantry list for Kitchen Season recommends checking and restocking staples as mid-November holiday cooking begins.
Baking ingredients and spices lose potency over time, so the author advises refreshing them regularly.
Spices and herbs are best bought in small quantities from bulk aisles to keep flavor at its peak.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Sixteen Austrian Wines You Should Try
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Delicious recommendations,including old favourites and new discoveries
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Austrian growers excel at freshness, elegance and drinkability, and the author tasted 72 Austrian wines in Amsterdam to select 16 favourites.
Fischer's Sauvignon Blanc St. Anna 2025 is made by brothers Klaus and Bernard, unfiltered with no additions, and priced at €25 from Joost Wijn in the Netherlands.
Franz Hofstätter's declassified Grüner Veltliner from the Achleiten vineyard in the Wachau is uncertified organic, with Weinskandal in Austria offering some Wabi Sabi wines.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Many Sins Of Wine Critics
NEWSLETTERS.summ: In the exciting (other adjectives are available) times we’re living in, we’re often told that writing is passé, people just don’t bother reading words anymore. A few journalistic outlets, especially in the financial press, seem to have finally come clean about the seriousness of their reporting, by auto-summarising their pieces...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin argues wine critics owe obligations only to those paying their bills, so consumers who dislike current reviewing can fund reviewers they prefer.
Atkin says the reviewing model's weakness is that tasting a wine in about 30 seconds, often among dozens, is too little assessment time.
He says conflicts of interest extend beyond payment to dining, friendships and shared politics, and that disclosing them can make advisers more self-interested.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Meet the Young Winemakers Reshaping Burgundy Right Now
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Meet the young winemakers in the heart of Burgundy who are tending the vines and shaping the future of wine
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: William Whitehead runs Domaine Michel Rebourgeon in Pommard, which works 4.25 hectares across Pommard, Volnay and Beaune and makes about 20,000 bottles a year.
Pierre Arcelain ages his white wine for 12 months in a concrete egg at Domaine Michel Arcelain, which is run with his wife Charlotte.
Arthur Thibert joined his father Pierre in Corgoloin in 2018, overseeing a new cuverie and more sustainable farming.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Find Rare Shizz With Orpheus Alerts!
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Some (more!) exciting news, folks: As many of you already know, sometimes wines get featured on here that are pretty rare. I’m talking about the kind of stuff that either doesn’t make it to the big platforms, or, if it does, is either priced astronomically or is gone in milliseconds. Understandably, that can be somewhat […]...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: 1WineDude is partnering with Orpheus Alerts, part of Orpheus Intelligence Labs Inc., to help buyers find rare wines.
Orpheus monitors sources like local-language catalogues, merchant inventories, auction and consignment notices, and private cellar sales.
Users create alerts using natural-language descriptions and optional images; Orpheus notifies them when matching wine is available and connects them with sellers.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Catalonia’s Under(wine)world
NEWSLETTERS.summ: How a Champagne trip in the 1800s resulted in a new Spanish wine in a league of its own
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: Josep Raventós's family, making wine since 1497, produced Spain's first traditional method sparkling wine in 1872 in Sant Sadurní d'Anoia, Penedès.
Cava is named after the cellars dug to store the wine, a term used informally from the 1960s and formalised under Spanish law in 1972.
Finca Sumarroca's 2022 Gran Reserva Brut Nature Cava, made from Macabeu, Xarel•lo and Parellada, aged 40 months and costs $28 Cdn.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Roadshow Review: Spain Brings Value Wines to China
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Does any nation offer better wine value than Spain? This seems obvious to French bottlers, who import major amounts of Spanish wine each year. Per
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: The Wines From Castilla, La Mancha Roadshow stopped in Beijing and was set to visit Guangzhou on November 6.
Spain ranked fifth for wine volume in China last year, narrowly behind Italy but a quarter of leader Australia, per WBO stats.
The author highlighted Piqueras' El Abuelo, a blend of Alicante Bouschet, Monastrell and Syrah, as a standout at the roadshow.
